title: Kernel Roulette: seqlen & arch-aware autotuner for prefill/decode flows
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Runtime currently chooses kernels with static heuristics that underperform on mixed workloads. Short-prefill bursts and heterogeneous GPU types cause suboptimal kernel choices, increasing median and tail latency in production.
Goal: Implement a lightweight, deployable autotuner ("Kernel Roulette") that selects kernels per-request using an exploration/exploitation policy conditioned on architecture and sequence-length features. The system should be safe by default (deterministic fallback path) and expose tunables for conservative exploration for high-SLA customers.
Scope:
- Feature vector: GPU family fingerprint (SM count, tensor-core support), model dtype/quantization profile, recent per-request seqlen, prefill vs decode phase, KV-cache hit probability estimate, short-term latency residual.
- Policy: Thompson-sampling + annealed-softmax "roulette" with adjustable exploration temperature and per-customer risk budget.
- Safety: bounded-exploration rules and guaranteed fallback to a conservative kernel that satisfies latency SLOs.
- Observability: per-decision telemetry (chosen kernel, predicted vs actual latency, token throughput, cost delta) and offline replay harness for regret measurement.
Success criteria:
- End-to-end median latency improvement >= 5% for mixed workloads in staging A/B.
- No customer-visible tail regressions (P99 increase < 1.5x for canary group).
- Mechanism to pin kernel decisions per-customer and to fully disable exploration.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel Roulette integrated into runtime decision path and selectable via feature flag
Per-request decision provenance logged and visible in Console trace view
Canary rollout plan validated: 5% canary with automated rollback on SLO breach
Offline replay harness (unit tests + dataset) to compute regret vs baseline present in repo
Benchmarks show >=5% median latency improvement on mixed prefills and no P99 regressions in canary
comments: 2025-02-06 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Drive (see references). Initial design favors a compact model-free bandit with light feature hashing to remain CPU-friendly in the request path.

2025-02-12 - Liam Chen: Prototype implemented: Thompson sampling with Beta priors per kernel variant. Instrumented microbench harness (runtime/tests/kernel_roulette_bench). Local microbench shows median improvement 7% on heterogeneous 8k/128 mixes, but saw 20% tail regressions on 32-token prefill cases.

2025-02-18 - Design review: Decided to add a stability estimator that suppresses exploration when observed latency variance for a kernel > 2x baseline. Also require per-customer exploration budget and opt-out flag for enterprise customers.
2025-02-21 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4689 (implements feature flag wiring, simple bandit engine, telemetry hooks). Requested reviewers: @maria-ops, @jamal-infra.

2025-02-26 - Benchmark run: staging/bench-2025-02-26 CSV uploaded. Summary: mixed workloads median -6.3%, P95 -3.5%. Short-prefill-heavy workloads showed P99 spikes; root cause traced to kernel warmstart behavior on small batches.

2025-03-03 - Liam Chen: Added conservative-explore mode and a warmstart burn-in for kernels with cold allocation overhead. Re-ran microbench: P99 tail improved to within 1.2x of baseline for problematic cases.

2025-03-08 - PM feedback (Rohit Desai): Add a customer-exposed toggle in Console and a rollout checklist for enterprise dedicated clusters. PM asks for explicit rollback threshold: +15% median or +25% P99 for canary group triggers immediate rollback.

2025-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Preparing canary rollout JIRA and runbook. Need SRE review for autoscaler interactions (possible oscillation when kernel choice changes throughput). Linked dependency ENG-27105 for occupancy projection work.
Next steps: finalize SRE safety net, complete code review, schedule 5% canary in staging with automated SLO checks, and add offline replay evaluation for historical traffic (dataset in references).
release_notes: Introduce 'Kernel Roulette' experimental autotuner behind a feature flag. Default off for enterprise tenants. Expected median latency improvement for mixed workloads; can be rolled back automatically on SLO breaches.
